title: Point probabilities of a biased random function
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p\in[0,1]$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Under the product probability law in which the values at distinct inputs are independent and each is true with probability $p$, the probability of obtaining exactly $f$ is the product, over all inputs $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, of the probability that a single bit equals $f(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean-valued function on the sign cube
